activities.anchor: hit by the same flood on the same night
activities.caption: one river, two towns — drag the divider between their outcomes
activities.name: emTownsCompare

config.prompt: One river, two towns — drag the divider between their flood nights:

before.label: town A — decided years early
before.text: Building codes raised floors above the flood line, a levee guards the business district, and the hospital's emergency plan was last exercised in May — so the evacuation runs by the book and the water does less damage.

after.label: town B — improvised on the day
after.text: Houses sit on the floodplain just as they always have, the emergency plan lives in a binder nobody has opened, and the response is improvised hour by hour.

config.why: The difference was made in the years before the flood, and in the years that will follow it — which is exactly where emergency management works.

activities.caption: structural or non-structural? file the mitigation
activities.name: emMitigationBuckets

config.prompt: Two families of mitigation — file each measure:
buckets: non-structural — shapes what humans put where

items.label: building codes that make new structures survive
land-use rules keeping development off floodplains
buyouts turning riverside parcels into parks
homes elevated above the flood line
insurance pricing that makes risk visible in the market

config.why: Even sandbags and boarded windows stacked before a hurricane count as structural — the family is defined by what it does, not when it happens.

activities.anchor: The economics are the discipline's loudest argument
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the mitigation multiplier
activities.name: emDollarEstimate

config.prompt: Rigorous benefit–cost analyses of federal mitigation grants found each dollar invested returns roughly how much in avoided future losses?
config.unit: dollars of avoided losses per dollar
config.why: Roughly six — and code adoption alone returns multiples of its cost over a building's life.
config.context: The Multi-Hazard Mitigation Council's landmark study, updated in 2019, is where the number comes from.

activities.anchor: Engineering against nature has a seduction problem
activities.caption: the levee is built — now decide like doctrine does
activities.name: emLeveeBranch

config.root: The wall is built and the land behind it feels safe. Development pressure arrives — decide.

start.text: A levee now guards the business district, and a developer eyes the floodplain behind it. Your call:

choices.label: Welcome the development — the levee protects
choices.feedback: This is how the seduction works: safety felt is risk concentrated — development pours in behind the wall.

choices.label: Pair the levee with land-use restraint — stop filling the floodplain
choices.feedback: Doctrine's pairing: structural works plus restraint, so the stakes behind the wall stop rising.

choices.label: Raise the levee higher instead
choices.feedback: Higher walls raise the stakes for the day one is overtopped — the problem is not the wall's height but the filling behind it.

dev.text: Years pass and houses thicken behind the levee. The day it is overtopped — New Orleans before 2005 is the canonical case — the concentrated stakes make the disaster worse.

ok.text: The floodplain stays open — parks, not houses. When the water comes, it floods land that can absorb it, and the town keeps what doctrine calls its second chance.

higher.text: Taller walls, fuller floodplains — the levee effect compounds: walls alone can concentrate the very risk they promise to remove.

config.why: Modern doctrine always pairs structural works with land-use restraint: build the levee, but also stop filling the floodplain behind it.

activities.anchor: not a capability — which is why
activities.caption: one line of the preparedness review is wrong — find it
activities.name: emPlanSpot

config.prompt: A town audits its readiness. One line is wrong — click it:
lines: The emergency operations plan pre-decides the questions a disaster will ask: who declares, who runs evacuation, where the EOC sits
Stockpiles and cache networks are positioned before the roads become impossible
The plan is printed, filed, and complete — the jurisdiction is prepared
Exercises run from tabletop discussions through drills to full-scale simulations
Each exercise ends with an after-action review that converts what went wrong into plan revisions
config.correction: A written-but-untested plan is paper — preparedness is a loop, not a filing cabinet.
config.why: Exercises carry as much weight as the plan itself: the gaps get named in a tabletop before the day discovers them.

activities.anchor: Its priorities are taught as a fixed triad
activities.caption: stack the response priorities in drilled order
activities.name: emTriadOrder

config.prompt: Response's priorities in order — the order that decides real choices:
config.why: The order is drilled because it decides choices under pressure — the crew that risks itself to protect property ahead of people is not doing response correctly.

activities.caption: true or false — recovery's two lessons
activities.name: emEquityJudge

statements.s: Disasters redistribute harm unevenly, and the households least able to absorb losses recover slowest.
statements.why: Who gets aid, how fast and with what conditions is an operational variable — recovery is where equity shows.

statements.s: Aid rules written for document-holding homeowners never leave anyone stranded.
statements.why: They strand renters and others — a design flaw, not a footnote.

statements.s: The rebuild window is the one moment when elevation, codes, relocation and infrastructure hardening are politically available.
statements.why: Everyone has just seen the flood line with their own eyes — recovery is mitigation's second chance.

statements.s: Recovery begins only after the response phase has fully ended.
statements.why: It begins during response, once the immediate threat to life has passed.

statements.s: A community that rebuilds identically has simply scheduled its next disaster.
statements.why: Closing the wheel without turning it — restoring function is the goal, restoring fragility is the failure.

activities.anchor: the moment that decides most casualty counts
activities.caption: fill the four tests a warning must pass
activities.name: emWarningCloze

config.text: A warning works only if it is %%0%% (does the siren reach everyone, including the deaf and the asleep?), %%1%% (does it say what will happen, where, when and what to do?), %%2%% (has the source earned credibility?) and %%3%% (people check with family and neighbours before acting).
config.hint: Technology predicts; people act on trust and comprehension — "Move to high ground now" beats "A flood event is anticipated".
